overview: The Desalination Technology for Coastal MSMEs (CSIR-CSMCRI) scheme focuses on providing desalination technology solutions to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in coastal regions. It aims to support sustainable water purification and resource utilization through indigenous membrane-based technologies developed by CSIR-CSMCRI. The scheme facilitates technology transfer, technical collaboration, and capacity building for MSMEs engaged in water treatment, desalination, and related industrial applications.
objectives: Provide cost-effective desalination technologies to coastal MSMEs
Promote sustainable water purification using membrane-based processes
Facilitate technology transfer of indigenously developed RO and UF systems
Support industrial wastewater treatment and zero liquid discharge (ZLD) solutions
Enhance capacity building through training and technical guidance
Encourage adoption of eco-friendly desalination and brine management technologies
Strengthen industry-institute collaboration for scalable water solutions
Enable recovery of valuable chemicals from desalination brines and waste streams
eligibility: MSMEs operating in coastal regions seeking desalination, water purification, or brine treatment technologies; must be engaged in industrial or commercial activities related to water treatment, desalination, or value recovery from saline waste streams; eligibility is subject to technical feasibility and alignment with CSIR-CSMCRI’s technology portfolio.
benefits: Access to indigenously developed reverse osmosis (RO), ultrafiltration (UF), nanofiltration, and electrodialysis technologies; technical support for plant design, installation, and operation; training on membrane maintenance and fouling mitigation; assistance in achieving zero liquid discharge (ZLD); recovery of valuable by-products like potash, magnesia, and bromine from brine; compliance with environmental standards for wastewater treatment.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through consultancy, sponsored projects, or technology transfer agreements on a case-by-case basis; costs are determined based on project scope, technology complexity, and scale of deployment; payment terms follow CSIR Guidelines for technology transfer and utilization of knowledgebase; no fixed grant or subsidy amount is specified in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant desalination or water purification technology from CSIR-CSMCRI’s portfolio. 2. Initiate contact via the Business Development & Information Management Division. 3. Submit a formal collaboration request outlining intended application and scale. 4. Undergo technical feasibility assessment by CSIR-CSMCRI experts. 5. Negotiate terms of technology transfer, consultancy, sponsored project. 6. Execute agreement and proceed with technology deployment, if applicable.
required_documents: Project proposal detailing intended application of technology
Site plan and water source analysis (if applicable)
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on project feasibility and mutual agreement.
implementing_agency: Central Salt & Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSIR-CSMCRI), Bhavnagar
caveats: Technology transfer is subject to evaluation of technical and commercial viability
Customization and scale-up may involve additional costs and timelines
Intellectual property rights remain with CSIR-CSMCRI unless otherwise negotiated
Post-installation training and support may be limited to agreed-upon terms
Availability of certain technologies depends on ongoing R&D and project status
